To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) social relations are interdependent and (b) the interdependencies among relations are not random but are structured.

(1) the social network is the basic unit of social analysis, (2) the global structure of the network is the key to understanding its functioning, (3) the global structure is the result of concatenation of local effects, (4) the global structure can be described by a functorial mapping, (5) the global structure consists of classes of individuals that are structurally equivalent, (6) structural equivalence can be described in terms of a set of algebraic properties of the network,
the structure of the relations in a social network can be represented as a functor from the category of relations to the category of graphs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a general problem of the social sciences, the analysis of the structure of social relations, in particular the structure of social networks, and with a mathematical problem in algebra, the analysis of homomorphisms of directed graphs.
the interrelations among interrelations within concrete social groups, and with the structural equivalence of individuals within such groups.
the structural equivalence of individuals in social networks, as well as the interrelations among these equivalences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of categories is a powerful tool for the study of social structure.
the social network is a 'functor'.
the social network approach is a powerful tool for the analysis of social structure, and that the functorial mapping of relations is a powerful tool in the analysis of social networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the social network approach, when properly formalized, provides a useful tool for the study of social structure.
we are seeking to establish a 'theory of social structure' which is not a theory of ideal types.
we are trying to understand social structures as they are, not as they are supposed to be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the algebraic theory of categories is useful in social science.
the notion of equivalence is central to the analysis of social relations, and that the algebraic theory of categories provides a powerful tool for this analysis.
social structure is a relational concept, which can be understood through the interrelations among social relations.
